title: The Book of Exodus Timeline
sub: Slavery to Sinai · God's Name and His Dwelling Place
desc: Ten plagues break Pharaoh's grip, a sea divides for Israel's escape, and at Sinai God gives his name, his law, and detailed plans for a tabernacle where he will live among his people: plans nearly wrecked by a golden calf before Moses's intercession saves the covenant.

eras.label: Era One · Exodus 1
eras.name: Israel Enslaved in Egypt
eras.dates: A new Pharaoh "who did not know about Joseph" turns Israel's prosperity into a threat, escalating from forced labor to a state order for infanticide: foiled by two midwives who fear God more than the king.

events.title: "Kill Every Son": the Midwives Defy Pharaoh
events.detail: As Israel multiplies rapidly in Egypt, a new king forgets Joseph's legacy and enslaves them with hard labor; when that fails to curb their growth, he orders Hebrew midwives to kill every son at birth, but Shiphrah and Puah let the boys live because they "feared God."

verses.text: “The midwives feared God [Elohim] and did not do what the king of Egypt had told them; they let the boys live.”

eras.label: Era Two · Exodus 2
eras.name: Moses Born, and Flees to Midian
eras.dates: A Levite baby hidden in a basket on the Nile is adopted by Pharaoh's own daughter, but his violent defense of a fellow Hebrew forces him to flee to Midian for decades before God even notices Israel's suffering.

events.title: A Basket on the Nile
events.detail: A Levite woman hides her son for three months, then sets him adrift in a papyrus basket on the Nile; Pharaoh's own daughter finds and adopts him, naming him Moses, unknowingly paying his own mother to nurse him.

events.title: Moses Flees to Midian
events.detail: Moses kills an Egyptian he sees beating a Hebrew, and when the act becomes known, he flees Pharaoh's wrath to Midian, where he marries Zipporah, the daughter of the priest Jethro.

events.title: God Hears the Groaning
events.detail: Egypt's king dies, but Israel's slavery continues; their cry finally reaches God, who remembers his covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob and takes notice of their suffering.

verses.text: “God [Elohim] heard their groaning; God [Elohim] remembered his covenant with Abraham, with Isaac, and with Jacob. God [Elohim] saw the Israelites, and God [Elohim] understood.”

eras.label: Era Three · Exodus 3
eras.name: The Burning Bush
eras.dates: A bush that burns without being consumed stops Moses in his tracks, and out of it comes both his commission to confront Pharaoh and God's own self-revelation of his personal name.

events.title: "I Have Surely Seen the Affliction of My People"
events.detail: The angel of the LORD appears to Moses in a bush ablaze but not consumed; God commissions him to bring Israel out of Egypt, promising "I will be with you" despite Moses's protest that he is no one important.

verses.text: “He said, ‘I am the God [Elohim] of your father, the God [Elohim] of Abraham, the God [Elohim] of Isaac, and the God [Elohim] of Jacob.’ Then Moses hid his face, because he was afraid to look at God [Elohim].”

events.title: "I AM Has Sent Me"
events.detail: Moses asks for a name to give the Israelites, and God answers with the enigmatic "I AM THAT I AM," then gives the personal name LORD, his memorial "from generation to generation", along with a prediction that Pharaoh will resist until forced, and that Israel will leave Egypt plundered rather than empty-handed.

verses.text: “God [Elohim] said to Moses, ‘I AM that I AM.’… God [Elohim] also said to Moses, ‘You must say this to the Israelites, “The LORD [Yahweh] — the God [Elohim] of your fathers… has sent me to you.” This is my name forever, and this is my memorial from generation to generation.’”

eras.label: Era Four · Exodus 4
eras.name: Signs for Moses, and a Deadly Night on the Road
eras.dates: God equips a reluctant Moses with three miraculous signs and a spokesman in Aaron, but an obscure, unsettling episode on the road home nearly costs Moses his life until Zipporah's quick action with a flint knife saves him.

events.title: Three Signs, and a Reluctant Prophet
events.detail: God gives Moses three signs to prove his commission (a staff turned to a snake, a hand turned leprous and healed, and water turned to blood) and, after Moses keeps protesting his inadequacy, assigns Aaron as his spokesman despite becoming angry at the repeated refusals.

events.title: "A Bridegroom of Blood": Zipporah's Quick Action
events.detail: On the road back to Egypt, the LORD unexpectedly seeks to kill Moses until Zipporah circumcises their son and touches the foreskin to Moses, an obscure act that satisfies whatever the danger was; Aaron then meets Moses, and the Israelite elders believe the signs and bow down in worship.

verses.text: “The LORD [Yahweh] met Moses and sought to kill him. But Zipporah took a flint knife, cut off the foreskin of her son and touched it to Moses' feet, and said, ‘Surely you are a bridegroom of blood to me.’”

eras.label: Era Five · Exodus 5
eras.name: "Who Is the LORD That I Should Obey Him?"
eras.dates: Moses and Aaron's first appeal to Pharaoh backfires immediately, not freedom, but a harsher workload, as Pharaoh strips away the straw for brickmaking while demanding the same daily quota.

events.title: Bricks Without Straw
events.detail: Pharaoh dismisses the LORD outright and punishes the request for a wilderness pilgrimage by withdrawing the straw supply while keeping brick quotas unchanged; the Israelite foremen, beaten for the shortfall, blame Moses and Aaron, and Moses himself questions why God sent him at all.

verses.text: “Pharaoh said, ‘Who is the LORD [Yahweh] that I should obey him by releasing Israel? I do not know the LORD [Yahweh], and I will not release Israel!’”

eras.label: Era Six · Exodus 6
eras.name: "I Am the LORD" — the Name Revealed to Moses
eras.dates: God answers Moses's discouragement with a fourfold covenant promise built entirely around the personal name LORD, followed by a genealogy confirming Moses and Aaron's own credentials as Levi's descendants.

events.title: "I Will Redeem You With an Outstretched Arm"
events.detail: God reveals that the patriarchs knew him as God Almighty but not by his personal name LORD, and promises with fourfold emphasis (I will bring out, I will rescue, I will redeem, I will take you as my people) though the discouraged Israelites do not listen.

verses.text: “God [Elohim] spoke to Moses and said to him, ‘I am the LORD [Yahweh]. I appeared to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob as God Almighty [El Shaddai], but by my name “the LORD” [Yahweh] I was not known to them.’”

events.title: The Family Line of Moses and Aaron
events.detail: A genealogy traces Reuben, Simeon, and especially Levi's line down through Amram to Moses and Aaron, establishing their credentials as the very men commissioned to confront Pharaoh.

eras.label: Era Seven · Exodus 7
eras.name: Aaron's Staff, and the Nile Turned to Blood
eras.dates: Aaron's staff swallowing the Egyptian magicians' own snake-staffs proves nothing to Pharaoh, and the first plague, the Nile itself turned to blood, changes nothing either, as God has already declared Pharaoh's heart will be hardened. (Hebrew verses 26-29 are numbered as most English Bibles' 8:1-4.)

events.title: Aaron's Staff Swallows the Magicians' Staffs
events.detail: God warns Moses that Pharaoh's heart will be hardened despite multiplied signs; Aaron's staff becomes a snake before Pharaoh and swallows the magicians' own staffs turned snakes, but Pharaoh's heart remains hard exactly as predicted.

events.title: The Nile Turned to Blood
events.detail: Aaron strikes the Nile with his staff and it turns to blood throughout Egypt, killing the fish and making the water undrinkable for seven days, yet the magicians replicate the sign with their own secret arts, and Pharaoh's heart stays hard. (Verses 26-29 numbered 8:1-4 in most English translations.)

verses.text: “This is what the LORD [Yahweh] has said: ‘By this you will know that I am the LORD [Yahweh]: I am going to strike the water of the Nile with the staff that is in my hand, and it will be turned into blood.’”

eras.label: Era Eight · Exodus 8
eras.name: Frogs, Gnats, and Flies
eras.dates: Three more plagues escalate the confrontation: frogs Pharaoh actually begs to have removed, gnats the magicians finally cannot replicate and call "the finger of God," and flies that spare Goshen entirely, proving the LORD's selective power. (Hebrew chapter 8 begins at what most English Bibles number as 8:5.)

events.title: Frogs Cover the Land
events.detail: Frogs swarm every corner of Egyptian life until Pharaoh begs Moses to pray them away, promising release in exchange: a promise he breaks the moment the plague ends. (Numbered 8:5-15 in most English translations.)

events.title: Gnats: "The Finger of God"
events.detail: Unlike the previous plagues, the magicians cannot replicate the plague of gnats and admit to Pharaoh, "It is the finger of God," yet Pharaoh's heart remains hardened regardless. (Numbered 8:16-19 in most English translations.)

verses.text: “The magicians said to Pharaoh, ‘It is the finger of God [Elohim]!’ But Pharaoh's heart remained hard, and he did not listen to them, just as the LORD [Yahweh] had predicted.” (Numbered 8:19 in most English translations.)

events.title: Flies, and a Line Drawn at Goshen
events.detail: Swarms of flies devastate Egypt while God explicitly spares Goshen, "so that you may know that I am the LORD in the midst of this land"; Pharaoh again promises release under pressure and again hardens his heart once the plague lifts. (Numbered 8:20-32 in most English translations.)

verses.text: “I will mark off the land of Goshen, where my people are staying, so that no swarms of flies will be there, that you may know that I am the LORD [Yahweh] in the midst of this land. I will put a division between my people and your people.” (Numbered 8:22-23 in most English translations.)

eras.label: Era Nine · Exodus 9
eras.name: Livestock, Boils, and Hail
eras.dates: The plagues turn personal and physical: Egypt's livestock dies while Israel's survives untouched, boils afflict even the magicians themselves, and hail devastates crops with a violence Egypt had never seen, finally extracting Pharaoh's admission "I have sinned."

events.title: Livestock Die, Israel's Survive
events.detail: A plague kills all of Egypt's livestock while sparing every animal belonging to Israel, a distinction so clear that Pharaoh sends investigators to confirm it, yet his heart stays hard regardless.

events.title: Boils on the Magicians Themselves
events.detail: Soot thrown into the air becomes festering boils across Egypt, afflicting even the magicians so severely they cannot even stand before Moses: the first plague God himself hardens Pharaoh's heart against, rather than Pharaoh hardening it himself.

events.title: "I Have Sinned This Time": Devastating Hail
events.detail: God warns this plague is meant "to show you my strength, and so that my name may be declared in all the earth"; hail mixed with fire devastates Egypt's fields and shatters trees, and Pharaoh finally confesses "I have sinned" and "the LORD is righteous", before hardening his heart yet again once the storm stops.

verses.text: “Pharaoh sent and summoned Moses and Aaron and said to them, ‘I have sinned this time! The LORD [Yahweh] is righteous, and I and my people are guilty. Pray to the LORD [Yahweh]… I will release you and you will stay no longer.’”

eras.label: Era Ten · Exodus 10
eras.name: Locusts and Darkness
eras.dates: Locusts devour whatever the hail spared, and a three-day darkness "so thick it can be felt" leaves Egyptians paralyzed in place while Israel alone has light: Pharaoh's final refusal ending in a threat against Moses's own life.

events.title: Locusts Devour What the Hail Left
events.detail: Even Pharaoh's own advisers press him to relent as locusts blanket Egypt and devour every green thing the hail spared; Pharaoh confesses sin again and begs forgiveness, but hardens his heart once more the moment the locusts are blown into the sea.

verses.text: “Pharaoh's servants said to him, ‘How long will this man be a menace to us? Release the people so that they may serve the LORD [Yahweh] their God [Elohim]. Do you not know that Egypt is destroyed?’”

events.title: Three Days of Darkness, and a Final Threat
events.detail: A darkness thick enough to feel paralyzes Egypt for three days while Israel has light in their own homes; Pharaoh's last offer (go, but leave the livestock) is rejected by Moses, and Pharaoh threatens to kill Moses if he ever sees his face again.

verses.text: “Pharaoh said to him, ‘Go from me! Watch out for yourself! Do not appear before me again, for when you see my face you will die!’ Moses said, ‘As you wish! I will not see your face again.’”

eras.label: Era Eleven · Exodus 11-12
eras.name: The Passover, and the Death of the Firstborn
eras.dates: The tenth and final plague strikes at midnight (every Egyptian firstborn dead, every Israelite household spared by lamb's blood on the doorframe) instituting the Passover as a perpetual memorial the same night Israel finally walks free.

events.title: "I Will Bring One More Plague"
events.detail: God announces the death of every Egyptian firstborn as the final, decisive plague, promising that afterward Pharaoh will not merely release Israel but drive them out completely.

verses.text: “Moses said, ‘This is what the LORD [Yahweh] has said: “About midnight I will go throughout Egypt, and all the firstborn in the land of Egypt will die, from the firstborn son of Pharaoh… to the firstborn son of the slave girl.”’”

events.title: The Passover Instituted
events.detail: Detailed instructions establish the Passover lamb, the blood on the doorframes as a sign against the destroyer, and unleavened bread eaten in haste: a ceremony Israel is commanded to observe "perpetually as a lasting ordinance" for every generation to come.

verses.text: “I will pass through the land of Egypt in the same night, and I will attack all the firstborn in the land of Egypt… The blood will be a sign for you on the houses where you are, so that when I see the blood I will pass over you.”

events.title: Midnight, and Israel's Departure
events.detail: At midnight the LORD strikes every Egyptian firstborn, and Pharaoh finally drives Israel out; roughly 600,000 men plus dependents leave with plundered Egyptian silver and gold, closing exactly 430 years after Israel first entered Egypt.

verses.text: “At the end of the 430 years, on the very day, all the regiments of the LORD [Yahweh] went out of the land of Egypt.”

eras.label: Era Twelve · Exodus 13
eras.name: Every Firstborn Consecrated, and the Pillar of Fire
eras.dates: Departing Israel is commanded to set apart every firstborn permanently as a living memorial of the exodus, while God himself leads the march visibly: a pillar of cloud by day, a pillar of fire by night, never once leaving their sight.

events.title: "Set Apart to Me Every Firstborn"
events.detail: God commands that every firstborn male, human and animal, be consecrated as a permanent reminder of the exodus, with clear instructions for children to ask about the ritual's meaning in future generations.

events.title: The Pillar of Cloud and Fire
events.detail: God deliberately avoids the shorter route through Philistine territory to prevent Israel from losing heart at the sight of war, and personally leads them with a visible pillar of cloud by day and fire by night that never leaves its place before the people.

verses.text: “The LORD [Yahweh] was going before them by day in a pillar of cloud to guide them on the way, and by night in a pillar of fire to give them light, so that they could travel day or night.”

eras.label: Era Thirteen · Exodus 14
eras.name: Crossing the Red Sea
eras.dates: Trapped between Pharaoh's pursuing army and the sea, Israel's terror turns to awe as the waters divide on dry ground, and close again over the entire Egyptian army the moment Israel reaches the other side.

events.title: "The LORD Will Fight for You"
events.detail: Pharaoh's heart hardens once more and he pursues the fleeing Israelites with his full army, trapping them against the sea; terrified, the people accuse Moses of bringing them out only to die, but Moses answers that the LORD himself will fight for them.

verses.text: “Moses said to the people, ‘Do not fear! Stand firm and see the salvation of the LORD [Yahweh] that he will provide for you today… The LORD [Yahweh] will fight for you, and you can be still.’”

events.title: The Sea Divided, and the Egyptian Army Destroyed
events.detail: Moses stretches his hand over the sea and an east wind divides the waters into a wall on either side; Israel crosses on dry ground, and when the pursuing Egyptian army follows, the waters return and destroy them completely, not one survives.

verses.text: “Israel saw the great power that the LORD [Yahweh] had exercised over the Egyptians, they feared the LORD [Yahweh], and they believed in the LORD [Yahweh] and in his servant Moses.”

eras.label: Era Fourteen · Exodus 15
eras.name: The Song of Moses, and Bitter Water at Marah
eras.dates: Israel's first act on the far shore is worship, an extended victory song celebrating the LORD as a warrior, before the euphoria collides almost immediately with the practical crisis of undrinkable water in the wilderness.

events.title: "The LORD Is a Warrior": the Song of the Sea
events.detail: Moses and all Israel sing an extended victory song celebrating the LORD's triumph over Pharaoh's army, asking "Who is like you among the gods?" before Miriam leads the women in an answering refrain with hand drums and dancing.

verses.text: “The LORD [Yahweh] is my strength and my song, and he has become my salvation. This is my God [El], and I will praise him, my father's God [Elohim], and I will exalt him.”
“Who is like you, O LORD [Yahweh], among the gods? Who is like you — majestic in holiness, fearful in praises, working wonders?”

events.title: Bitter Water Made Sweet at Marah
events.detail: Three days after the sea's miracle, Israel already murmurs over bitter water at Marah; the LORD shows Moses a tree that sweetens it, then declares himself their healer if they obey, before the group finds relief at Elim's twelve springs and seventy palm trees.

verses.text: “If you will diligently obey the LORD [Yahweh] your God [Elohim], and do what is right in his sight… all the diseases that I brought on the Egyptians I will not bring on you, for I, the LORD [Yahweh], am your healer.”

eras.label: Era Fifteen · Exodus 16
eras.name: Manna and Quail
eras.dates: Hunger turns the euphoric Israelites nostalgic for Egyptian slavery, and God responds not with rebuke but daily bread from heaven: a test of obedience built into the very mechanics of gathering it, including a weekly rehearsal of Sabbath rest.

events.title: "I Am Going to Rain Bread From Heaven"
events.detail: Israel's hunger produces nostalgic complaints about Egypt's "pots of meat"; God provides quail in the evening and a flaky bread-like substance each morning, testing obedience through a rule that hoarded portions rot overnight except before the Sabbath.

verses.text: “The LORD [Yahweh] said to Moses, ‘I am going to rain bread from heaven for you, and the people will go out and gather the amount for each day, so that I may test them. Will they walk in my law or not?’”

events.title: A Sabbath Rehearsal, and an Omer Kept for Generations
events.detail: The sixth day's double portion stays fresh overnight specifically for the Sabbath, teaching Israel to rest on the seventh day even before the Ten Commandments formalize it; an omer of manna is preserved permanently before the ark as a reminder of the forty years Israel would eat it in the wilderness.

eras.label: Era Sixteen · Exodus 17
eras.name: Water From the Rock, and War With Amalek
eras.dates: Thirst provokes water struck from solid rock at Massah and Meribah, and Israel's first military battle turns on the literal position of Moses's raised hands: held up by Aaron and Hur until sunset secures victory.

events.title: "Is the LORD Among Us or Not?"
events.detail: Israel's thirst at Rephidim turns into open testing of God; Moses strikes the rock at Horeb with his staff and water flows out, and the place is named Massah and Meribah for the people's quarreling and testing.

events.title: Moses's Raised Hands Win the Battle
events.detail: Amalek attacks Israel at Rephidim, and the battle's outcome tracks the literal position of Moses's hands on the hilltop (raised, Israel prevails; lowered, Amalek gains ground) until Aaron and Hur hold his arms steady until sunset secures the victory.

verses.text: “Whenever Moses would raise his hands, then Israel prevailed, but whenever he would rest his hands, then Amalek prevailed. When the hands of Moses became heavy… Aaron and Hur held up his hands, one on one side and one on the other, and so his hands were steady until the sun went down.”

eras.label: Era Seventeen · Exodus 18
eras.name: Jethro's Advice — Delegated Justice
eras.dates: Moses's father-in-law watches him single-handedly judge every dispute in Israel from morning to evening and offers the practical fix that becomes Israel's entire judicial structure: capable men appointed over tens, fifties, hundreds, and thousands.

events.title: "What You Are Doing Is Not Good"
events.detail: Jethro reunites Moses with his wife and sons, rejoices at the LORD's deliverance of Israel, then watches Moses exhaust himself judging every dispute alone; his advice to appoint capable, God-fearing judges over smaller units, bringing only the hardest cases to Moses, becomes the working structure of Israel's justice system.

verses.text: “You choose from the people capable men, God-fearing men, men of truth, those who hate bribes, and put them over the people as rulers of thousands, rulers of hundreds, rulers of fifties, and rulers of tens.”

eras.label: Era Eighteen · Exodus 19
eras.name: Arrival at Sinai — "A Kingdom of Priests"
eras.dates: Israel arrives at the mountain where their story with God began, and the covenant offer that follows is conditional and reciprocal: Israel's special status as a kingdom of priests depends entirely on keeping what the LORD commands.

events.title: "You Will Be My Special Possession"
events.detail: God proposes a covenant built on Israel's obedience (a treasured possession, a kingdom of priests, a holy nation among all peoples) and the people answer unanimously, "All that the LORD has commanded we will do!" before three days of consecration prepare them to meet God at the mountain.

verses.text: “If you will diligently listen to me and keep my covenant, then you will be my special possession out of all the nations… and you will be to me a kingdom of priests and a holy nation.”

events.title: Thunder, Fire, and Boundaries Around the Mountain
events.detail: Mount Sinai erupts in thunder, lightning, smoke, and a trumpet blast so loud the whole camp trembles; strict boundaries are set that anyone, human or animal, who touches the mountain must die, underscoring the holiness of what is about to happen.

eras.label: Era Nineteen · Exodus 20
eras.name: The Ten Commandments
eras.dates: God speaks the foundational moral law directly to the assembled nation (worship, image-making, the divine name, Sabbath, family, and the sanctity of life, property, truth, and desire) terrifying the people into asking Moses to be their go-between from then on.

events.title: "I, the LORD, Am Your God": the First Four Commandments
events.detail: God opens the Ten Commandments by grounding every subsequent demand in the exodus itself, then forbids other gods, carved images, misusing the divine name, and finally commands Sabbath rest patterned directly on God's own rest at creation.

verses.text: “I, the LORD [Yahweh], am your God [Elohim], who brought you from the land of Egypt, from the house of slavery. You shall have no other gods before me.”

events.title: The Remaining Six Commandments, and the People's Fear
events.detail: The commandments turn from God to neighbor, honoring parents, and prohibitions on murder, adultery, theft, false witness, and covetousness; the terrified people beg Moses to mediate directly with God from then on rather than hear the divine voice themselves.

verses.text: “They said to Moses, ‘You speak to us and we will listen, but do not let God speak with us, lest we die.’”

eras.label: Era Twenty · Exodus 21-23
eras.name: The Book of the Covenant
eras.dates: Three dense chapters of case law apply the Ten Commandments to everyday disputes (slavery, personal injury, property damage, social justice for the poor and the foreigner, and Israel's festival calendar) closing with a promise of an angel to guide the nation into the land.

events.title: Laws on Servitude and Personal Injury
events.detail: Detailed case law governs Hebrew servants' release after six years, capital penalties for deliberate violence, and the principle of proportionate compensation for injury ("eye for eye, tooth for tooth") including specific rules for an ox that gores someone. (Verse 37 numbered 22:1 in most English translations.)

verses.text: “If there is serious injury, then you will give a life for a life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot, burn for burn, wound for wound, bruise for bruise.”

events.title: Property, Restitution, and Care for the Vulnerable
events.detail: Laws cover theft and restitution, negligence with fire or borrowed property, seduction, and sorcery, before turning explicitly to social ethics: a direct prohibition on wronging foreigners, widows, or orphans, grounded in Israel's own memory of oppression in Egypt. (Numbered 22:2-31 in most English translations.)

verses.text: “You must not wrong a resident foreigner nor oppress him, for you were foreigners in the land of Egypt. You must not afflict any widow or orphan.” (Numbered 22:21-22 in most English translations.)

events.title: Justice, Sabbath Years, and the Three Annual Feasts
events.detail: Laws demand impartial justice even toward an enemy's straying animal, institute a sabbatical year of rest for the land, and establish Israel's three annual pilgrim feasts: Unleavened Bread, Harvest, and Ingathering.

verses.text: “You must not oppress a resident foreigner, since you know the life of a foreigner, for you were foreigners in the land of Egypt.”

events.title: An Angel to Guide Them Into the Land
events.detail: God promises to send an angel bearing his own name and authority to guide Israel into Canaan, gradually driving out its inhabitants "little by little" so the land will not become desolate, on the strict condition that Israel makes no covenant with the nations or their gods.

verses.text: “I am going to send an angel before you to protect you as you journey and to bring you into the place that I have prepared. Take heed because of him, and obey his voice… for my Name is in him.”

eras.label: Era Twenty-One · Exodus 24
eras.name: The Covenant Ratified
eras.dates: Blood splashed on both the altar and the people seals the covenant formally, and seventy elders climb the mountain to see God and share a meal in his presence before Moses disappears into the cloud for forty days.

events.title: "The Blood of the Covenant"
events.detail: Moses reads the Book of the Covenant aloud and the people commit to obey; he splashes sacrificial blood on both the altar and the people to seal the covenant, and seventy elders ascend the mountain, see God, and eat a meal in his presence before Moses enters the cloud for forty days and nights.

verses.text: “Moses took the blood and splashed it on the people and said, ‘This is the blood of the covenant that the LORD [Yahweh] has made with you in accordance with all these words.’”

eras.label: Era Twenty-Two · Exodus 25-27
eras.name: Blueprints for the Tabernacle
eras.dates: Precise, exhaustive instructions specify every dimension and material for the ark, table, lampstand, tabernacle structure, and bronze altar: a portable dwelling place built exactly to a pattern God shows Moses on the mountain.

events.title: The Ark, the Table, and the Golden Lampstand
events.detail: God calls for a freewill offering of materials and specifies exact dimensions for the gold-covered ark with its cherubim-topped atonement lid, the table for the Bread of the Presence, and the seven-branched golden lampstand: "according to all that I am showing you… you must make it exactly so."

verses.text: “Let them make for me a sanctuary, so that I may live among them. According to all that I am showing you… you must make it exactly so.”

events.title: The Tabernacle's Curtains and Frames
events.detail: Detailed specifications cover the linen and goat-hair curtains, acacia-wood frames with silver bases, and the special curtain separating the Holy Place from the Most Holy Place where the ark will rest.

events.title: The Bronze Altar and the Courtyard
events.detail: Instructions specify the hollow, bronze-covered altar for burnt offerings and the linen hangings enclosing the tabernacle's outer courtyard, closing with the command for a perpetually burning lamp "from evening to morning before the LORD."

eras.label: Era Twenty-Three · Exodus 28-29
eras.name: Priestly Garments and Ordination
eras.dates: Aaron and his sons receive elaborate ceremonial garments, an ephod bearing Israel's twelve tribes on his shoulders and over his heart, followed by a detailed seven-day ordination ritual involving blood applied to ear, thumb, and toe.

events.title: Holy Garments "for Glory and for Beauty"
events.detail: Aaron's priestly garments include a jeweled breastpiece bearing all twelve tribes' names over his heart, an ephod with onyx stones on his shoulders, and a gold plate reading "Holiness to the LORD" on his turban: vestments the text says are made "for glory and for beauty."

verses.text: “Aaron will bear the names of the sons of Israel in the breastpiece of decision over his heart when he goes into the Holy Place, for a memorial before the LORD [Yahweh] continually… Aaron is to bear the decisions of the Israelites over his heart before the LORD [Yahweh] continually.”

events.title: Seven Days of Ordination
events.detail: A detailed ordination ritual consecrates Aaron and his sons over seven days (washing, vesting, anointing, and blood applied to their right ear, thumb, and big toe) closing with God's promise to reside among the Israelites permanently as their God.

verses.text: “I will reside among the Israelites, and I will be their God [Elohim], and they will know that I am the LORD [Yahweh] their God [Elohim], who brought them out from the land of Egypt, so that I may reside among them.”

eras.label: Era Twenty-Four · Exodus 30-31
eras.name: The Incense Altar, Census Tax, and Bezalel's Calling
eras.dates: Final tabernacle instructions cover the incense altar, an atonement tax collected at every census, and sacred anointing oil, before God names the two craftsmen, Bezalel and Oholiab, specifically filled with his Spirit to execute the whole design.

events.title: Incense, Atonement Money, and Sacred Oil
events.detail: Instructions specify the gold incense altar, a half-shekel atonement tax collected equally from rich and poor at every census, the bronze basin for priestly washing, and a uniquely formulated anointing oil and incense forbidden for any other use.

events.title: Bezalel Filled With the Spirit of God, and the Sabbath Sign
events.detail: God specifically names and fills Bezalel and Oholiab with his own Spirit for the skill needed to execute every tabernacle detail, then reaffirms the Sabbath as a perpetual covenant sign before giving Moses the two stone tablets "written by the finger of God."

verses.text: “I have filled him with the Spirit of God [Elohim] in skill, in understanding, in knowledge, and in all kinds of craftsmanship.”
“He gave Moses two tablets of testimony when he had finished speaking with him on Mount Sinai, tablets of stone written by the finger of God [Elohim].”

eras.label: Era Twenty-Five · Exodus 32
eras.name: The Golden Calf
eras.dates: While Moses is still on the mountain receiving the law, Israel melts down its jewelry into an idol and calls it their god: a betrayal so severe that God offers to start over with Moses alone, and only Moses's intercession spares the nation.

events.title: "Leave Me Alone So That My Anger Can Burn"
events.detail: Impatient at Moses's delay, Israel pressures Aaron into casting a golden calf and calling it the god who brought them from Egypt; God's anger is so severe he proposes destroying the nation and starting over through Moses alone, but Moses's intercession, appealing to God's own promises to Abraham, turns God from that judgment.

verses.text: “The LORD [Yahweh] said to Moses, ‘I have seen this people. Look what a stiff-necked people they are! So now, leave me alone so that my anger can burn against them and I can destroy them, and I will make from you a great nation.’”
“The LORD [Yahweh] relented over the evil that he had said he would do to his people.”

events.title: The Tablets Shattered, and 3,000 Die
events.detail: Moses smashes the stone tablets in fury at the sight of the calf, burns and grinds the idol into powder for the people to drink, and orders the Levites to execute the ringleaders (about 3,000 die) before pleading with God a second time and offering his own life in exchange for the nation's forgiveness.

verses.text: “Moses returned to the LORD [Yahweh] and said, ‘Alas, this people has committed a very serious sin… But now, if you will forgive their sin…, but if not, wipe me out from your book that you have written.’”

eras.label: Era Twenty-Six · Exodus 33
eras.name: "Show Me Your Glory"
eras.dates: God's threat to send Israel on without his own presence devastates the camp, and Moses's intercession escalates into the boldest request in the book: to see God's glory directly, granted only in part, from a cleft in the rock.

events.title: "I Will Not Go Up Among You"
events.detail: God threatens to send Israel to Canaan led only by an angel rather than his own presence, calling them "a stiff-necked people" he might destroy along the way; Moses pitches a separate tent of meeting outside the camp where the LORD speaks with him "face to face, the way a person speaks to a friend."

verses.text: “The LORD [Yahweh] would speak to Moses face to face, the way a person speaks to a friend.”

events.title: "Show Me Your Glory"
events.detail: Moses presses for assurance that God's own presence, not just an angel, will go with Israel, securing the promise "my presence will go with you," then boldly asks to see God's glory directly; God agrees to let his goodness pass by while hiding Moses in a rock cleft, since "no one can see me and live."

verses.text: “The LORD [Yahweh] said, ‘My presence will go with you, and I will give you rest.’”

“I will make all my goodness pass before your face, and I will proclaim the LORD [Yahweh] by name before you; I will be gracious to whom I will be gracious; I will show mercy to whom I will show mercy.”

eras.label: Era Twenty-Seven · Exodus 34
eras.name: New Tablets, and the LORD's Name Proclaimed
eras.dates: Fresh stone tablets replace the shattered ones, and as the LORD passes by, he proclaims his own character aloud (compassionate, gracious, patient, loyal, but never leaving the guilty unpunished) the fullest self-description God gives anywhere in the Torah.

events.title: "The LORD, the LORD, Compassionate and Gracious"
events.detail: Moses cuts new stone tablets, and as the LORD passes by him he proclaims his own name and character in full: compassionate, gracious, slow to anger, abounding in loyal love and faithfulness, forgiving iniquity, yet by no means leaving the guilty unpunished.

verses.text: “The LORD [Yahweh] passed by before him and proclaimed: ‘The LORD [Yahweh], the LORD [Yahweh], the compassionate and gracious God [El], slow to anger, and abounding in loyal love and faithfulness, keeping loyal love for thousands, forgiving iniquity and transgression and sin. But he by no means leaves the guilty unpunished.’”

events.title: The Covenant Renewed, and Moses's Radiant Face
events.detail: God renews the covenant with warnings against alliances with Canaan's nations and a summary of festival law already given; after forty days on the mountain without food or water, Moses comes down with his face so radiant from being in God's presence that he must wear a veil except when speaking with the LORD.

verses.text: “When Aaron and all the Israelites saw Moses, the skin of his face shone, and they were afraid to approach him.”

eras.label: Era Twenty-Eight · Exodus 35-36
eras.name: The Freewill Offering, and Construction Begins
eras.dates: Israel's response to the tabernacle appeal is so overwhelming (willing hearts bringing gold, silver, and fine linen without being asked twice) that Moses has to issue an order telling the people to stop giving.

events.title: "Everyone Whose Heart Stirred Him"
events.detail: Moses relays the tabernacle instructions to the full community, and men and women alike respond with overwhelming, voluntary generosity (jewelry, fine yarns, and skilled labor) while God's naming of Bezalel and Oholiab as its craftsmen is repeated for the assembled people.

verses.text: “Everyone whose heart stirred him to action and everyone whose spirit was willing came and brought the offering for the LORD [Yahweh] for the work of the tent of meeting.”

events.title: "Too Much": the Offering Restrained
events.detail: The offerings pour in so far beyond what is needed that Moses has to order the people to stop bringing more, a detail found nowhere else in the wilderness narrative; construction of the tabernacle's curtains and frames then proceeds exactly as specified.

verses.text: “The people are bringing much more than is needed for the completion of the work which the LORD commanded us to do!… Let no man or woman do anymore work for the offering for the sanctuary.”

eras.label: Era Twenty-Nine · Exodus 37-39
eras.name: The Tabernacle's Furnishings Completed
eras.dates: Bezalel and his craftsmen execute every earlier instruction with exacting precision (the ark, table, lampstand, altars, courtyard, and priestly garments) each piece checked off with the same refrain: "just as the LORD had commanded Moses."

events.title: Bezalel Builds the Ark, Table, and Lampstand
events.detail: Bezalel personally constructs the gold-covered ark with its cherubim, the table for the Bread of the Presence, the golden lampstand, and the incense altar, matching the earlier blueprint detail for detail.

events.title: The Bronze Altar, the Courtyard, and a Full Inventory
events.detail: The bronze altar, the basin made from the mirrors of serving women, and the courtyard's linen hangings are completed, closing with a precise inventory of every talent and shekel of gold, silver, and bronze used in the entire project.

events.title: The Priestly Garments Finished: "Exactly So"
events.detail: The ephod, breastpiece, robe, and sacred garments are completed exactly as specified and brought to Moses for inspection; he examines every piece against the LORD's original instructions and, finding it done "exactly so," blesses the workers.

verses.text: “The Israelites did all the work according to all that the LORD [Yahweh] had commanded Moses. Moses inspected all the work, and they had done it just as the LORD [Yahweh] had commanded — they had done it exactly — and Moses blessed them.”

eras.label: Era Thirty · Exodus 40
eras.name: The Tabernacle Erected, and the Glory Fills It
eras.dates: Exodus closes exactly where it aimed all along: God's own presence dwelling visibly among his people, so overwhelming that even Moses cannot enter the finished tabernacle once the glory of the LORD fills it.

events.title: Moses Sets Up the Tabernacle
events.detail: On the first day of the new year, Moses assembles the tabernacle piece by piece exactly as commanded (frames, curtains, the ark, the table, the lampstand, the altars) anointing and consecrating each item and Aaron's priestly family along with it.

events.title: The Glory of the LORD Fills the Tabernacle
events.detail: The cloud covers the tent of meeting and the glory of the LORD fills the tabernacle so completely that even Moses cannot enter it: the visible fulfillment of God's promise to dwell among his people, with the cloud's movement guiding every stage of Israel's ongoing wilderness journey.

verses.text: “The cloud covered the tent of meeting, and the glory of the LORD [Yahweh] filled the tabernacle. Moses was not able to enter the tent of meeting because the cloud settled on it and the glory of the LORD [Yahweh] filled the tabernacle.”
